todaysEvents.summary: Iran says Hormuz still fully blocked
todaysEvents.delta: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority posted on X that US claims the strait has reopened 'do not change the reality' - it remains blocked until Tehran's conditions are accepted (CNBC, Aug 13).

Kpler data show vessel transits averaging 13/day over the five days to Aug 11, about 90% below the pre-war 130/day baseline and nearing the lowest level since May 12 (Investing.com/Yahoo Finance, Aug 13).

todaysEvents.summary: Analysts split on odds of imminent deal
todaysEvents.delta: Foreign policy analyst Charles Kupchan dismissed the Trump-Iran reparations rhetoric as 'back-and-forth banter,' noting both sides have economic and political incentive to reach a deal soon (CNBC, Aug 12-13).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and the US move toward a workable framework normalising Hormuz transit, but Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority still insisted on Aug 13 that the strait 'remains blocked' until Tehran's conditions - an end to the naval blockade, sanctions relief, reparations - are met, while Trump counter-demands compensation from Iran; a near-term signed reopening remains unlikely (CNBC, Aug 13). Brent moves toward $75-85 as the risk premium eases, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable full-reopening agreement emerges: Iran maintains its blockade-end, sanctions-relief and reparations conditions, Trump continues to counter-demand compensation from Iran, and Hormuz traffic keeps thinning - Kpler data show a five-day average of just 13 transits/day through Aug 11, near the lowest level since May 12 and about 90% below the pre-war baseline (Investing.com/Yahoo Finance, Aug 13). Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The compensation standoff hardens further, Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority keeps disputing US claims of control, and traffic keeps sinking toward the lows last seen in mid-May, raising the risk of a renewed full closure and spillover into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.
